newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Social Democrats call for markets to serve people.
newsitem.headline: Social Democrats call for markets to serve people.

text.p: Calling for markets to serve people and not vice versa, the Socialist International opened its 20th Congress at the United Nations on Monday with leaders emphasising social justice and greater opportunity.

Chaired by French former Prime Minister Pierre Mauroy, who was expected to receive a second term as president, the gathering includes heads of government, cabinet ministers and parliamentarians from 150 social democratic and labour parties from as far away as Mongolia.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said that beyond ideological consideration the social issues raised by the movement, which meets every four years, were also of fundamental concern to the United Nations.

"We cannot accept that the world, advancing ever more rapidly in progress and development, should leave by the wayside more than a billion men, women and children, living lives of utter despair," Boutros-Ghali said.

Mauroy said membership of the Group of Seven industrial countries should be enlarged and the socialist movement must be more active in combatting dictatorship and strengthening democracy around the world.

Japan's Labour Minister Takanobu Nagai said a social system was more necessary than ever to "control the deregulation process," adding: "So the mission for social democrats and socialists (is) for building a market economy that is better utilized for protecting the lives and rights of people."
In Japan, as in the United States, jobs are moved out of the country to nations where wages are lower. He said Japan should introduce programmes that would expand jobs at home.

Among participants are Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland, Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres, Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson and Mongolian Parliamentary President Radnaasumbereliin Gonchigdorj.
